Exercise A

A Summer in the National Parks

Read the text about young volunteers in the West. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading Text

Every summer, teenagers from all over the USA travel west to work as 1 in the national parks. They do not get any 2 for their work, but they get free food and a place to sleep.

In Alaska, one group helps to clean the 3 after big storms. Another group builds new 4 for walkers in the mountains.

The young people enjoy working outside, and they also learn a lot about 5 and how to protect it.

In the evening they sit around a 6 and talk about their day. Many say it is hard 7, but they never forget the 8.

Exercise B

Gerunds after Verbs: verb + -ing

After these verbs we use the gerund (verb + -ing): enjoy, finish, mind, suggest, avoid, practise, keep, give up.

Complete the Sentence

1. I enjoy in the mountains before breakfast.

2. She finished the tent at six o'clock.

3. Do you mind the dishes tonight?

4. Our guide suggested the beach on Saturday.

5. We avoid plastic bottles in the park.

6. The volunteers practise English with the visitors.

7. Keep and we will finish the path today.

8. He gave up television during the trip.

Exercise C

Gerunds after Prepositions: preposition + -ing

After a preposition (at, in, of, for, before, after, to, without) the verb always takes -ing.

Complete the Sentence

1. She is good at maps.

2. The volunteers are interested in the environment.

3. Instead of the bus, we walked back to the camp.

4. Thank you for us with the tents.

5. Before home, we cleaned the kitchen.

6. After the path, everybody was tired but happy.

7. We look forward to Alaska again next year.

8. He left the camp without goodbye.

Exercise D

Writing: A Project for Me

Write about a volunteering project you would like to join (6–8 sentences). Say what you enjoy doing, what you are good at, and what you would avoid. Use at least four gerunds.

Useful language
You can use these: I enjoy ...-ing I am good at ...-ing I am interested in ...-ing I don't mind ...-ing I would avoid ...-ing I look forward to ...-ing before ...-ing after ...-ing
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences with at least four gerunds (verb + -ing).
